Sorry to hear of your data loss. One thing that others can learn from this - installing an additional operating system usually involves creating or modifying partitions on your drive. It is vital to insure that we have good backups of all data before starting. This is true any time disk partitions are changed, not only when performing a dual-boot installation. There are ways to resize partitions non-destructively, but it is best to be cautious. Again, sorry for the lost data, but congratulations on having an awesome attitude about the whole thing. Good luck with your new Linux install.

You already know this now, but this is why I think it's vital to physically remove the connection to the backup once it's validated.
I really should've seen that coming. I definitely will next time.

There are several Linux data rescue utilities which might get your data back if you didn't do anything too drastic.

Safecopy and Ddrescue are two prime examples.

Those tools are to rescue data from failing devices. If the hdd is not damaged (it isn't because he installed linux) a simple dd can make an image of the disk. And you actually don't need to make an image of the disk to rescue deleted data.

If the old filesystem tables have been overwritten (I'm quite sure they have because they are at the beginning of the partition), recovering files is quite hard. Although there are a few programs to recover some specific files by searching the hdd for some magic numbers, but don't expect much from that.
